text: Start with Lamine. Seven league goals already, across four consecutive scoring appearances. Two against Rayo. Two at Valencia. Two at Levante. Then another against Racing. The player you worry about creating the chance is now finishing plenty of them himself. That changes the calculation for a defender. Give him room outside the box, and he can shoot. Rush into the challenge, and you give him the chance to take you out of the move. Send help, and somebody has left another area. Against Feyenoord, he even added a free kick. There is no single instruction that makes all of that disappear. Of course he can have quieter games. Every attacker can. The point is that containing his dribbling does not automatically contain his influence. And the more attention you commit to that side of the pitch, the more important it becomes to notice the player arriving somewhere else.
